text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday:
- Osijek-Baranja county authorities to prevent sales of its unprocessed wheat because that would leave local companies without raw materials.
- Zagreb town's assembly ceases to cooperate with the mayor and city government as of today, after expiry of ten-day ultimatum it set to resolve the long crisis.
- Croatia says it will not pay demanded 30 million German marks per year for deconstruction of a mutualy owned nuclear plant Krsko in Slovenia until new inter-state contract is signed.
- European Bank for Reconstruction signes contract on ivesting 20,000 German marks to finance private companies and small business.
- Owner of plush hotel Mozart in Istria plans to establish a new chain by reconstructing 15 existing hotels along the coast to be included in the luxurious "Klasic" chain.
- The race for stakes in Dalmatian coastal hotels has begun, but some banks already became majority owners of several tourist facilities.
- Introduction of the value added tax in Januray will have a hard impact on liquidity until the first circle of purchase, production nad sale is finished.
- Biggest Croatian insurer Croatia Osiguranje says its profits rose by 60 percent in this year's first six months.
- Owning a flat became a dream beyond reach of many as saquare meter costs between 1,200 and 4,500 German marks. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
